report.headline: Usage projected to shrink from 24.4% to 19.4%, with a prediction band wide enough to rank but not pinpoint him; shooting projection is not to be trusted at all

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 19.4% in the NBA, down from a EuroLeague usage rate of 24.4% (+0.96 sd above the EuroLeague average that season).

risks.text: His turnover rate in the source season was 18.6%, a notable cost alongside the high assist numbers.
The usage projection's own historical accuracy is limited: mean absolute error of 3.3% over 367 held-out transitions, only modestly better than the 4.3% error of simply guessing the league mean.

The true shooting projection of 53.0% is unreliable by the model's own accounting — its error (4.7%) is tied with the trivial league-mean baseline (4.7%), so no shooting efficiency conclusion should be drawn from it.
The estimate for this transition type rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA cases, a modest sample for a role change this large.

strengths.text: He carried a heavy offensive role in the EuroLeague, with usage at 24.4%, nearly a full standard deviation above the league average (+0.96 sd).
His EuroLeague production was playmaking-heavy: an assist rate of 32.5% and 7.058 assists per 75 possessions.
He belongs to a cohort of EL->NBA movers who, on average, sat +0.46 sd above their own league before making the jump, indicating the move followed a track record of standing out.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 14.2% to 24.7%, a span of roughly 10.5 points against an NBA usage standard deviation of 5.2% — about two standard deviations wide — so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot price his exact role. The true shooting projection of 53.0% should be ignored entirely: its out-of-fold error of 4.7% is no better than simply guessing the league mean (also 4.7% error), so it carries no information beyond that baseline.
